$comment: Codex CLI on a ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Business plan.
Like the Google file, `cache.kind` is `unpriced` - but for a different reason worth keeping
distinct, because the two would otherwise look like the same gap.
OpenAI does publish a cached-input discount on API pricing, and caching there is automatic
rather than something a client marks up or keeps alive. There is no TTL a scheduler can extend,
no write multiplier to pay, and therefore no keepalive move to make: the thing agentyard's cache
clock exists to manage is not exposed here. Pricing it would not make the clock work; it would
make it act on a lever that does not connect to anything.
So: a worker on this model runs work, is preempted at a window boundary, and hands off. It never
pays to hold a cache open, because on this provider nothing is held.
MODELS: read from $CODEX_HOME/models_cache.json on 2026-08-25 (codex-cli 0.149.1), which the CLI
refreshes itself. `gpt-reserve` and `codex-auto-review` are deliberately omitted: the first is not
a model an operator should route to by name, and the second is the review agent rather than a

cache.$comment: Caching is automatic and server-side; no client-controlled TTL, so no keepalive lever.

$comment: Codex has compaction in its session lifecycle, but no documented way to drive it from a
headless run. The adapter declares manualCompact: false deliberately - claiming a capability
that turns out to be absent strands a session at a window boundary, while omitting one that
is present costs only a missed optimisation.

quota.$comment: No non-interactive status command exists; openai/codex#10233 is the open request.

$owed: Whether headless compaction is reachable at all. If it is, manualCompact flips to true and moves 4 and 5 of the cache clock become available on this provider.
Context windows are documented figures; models_cache.json reports slugs, display names and effort levels but no window size.
Whether a subscription exposes any usage signal at all. `codex doctor --json` reports auth and health but nothing about remaining quota.
Whether rollout JSONL carries per-turn token usage in a shape transcript.ts can meter. If not, runs on this adapter are unmetered - HANDOFF R10.
